newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares close at record, AEX baulks at 600.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares close at record, AEX baulks at 600.

text.p: Dutch shares end Tuesday at a fresh closing high, the second in two days, but well short of a new intra-day high after coming close to breaking through the 600 level on AEX share index for the first time ever.
The index closed 0.49 points higher at 597.59, after climbing to 599.69 in the opening hours of the session, buoyed by another record high closing overnight on Wall Street.

Dealers said market makers were blocking off the way to 600 on the AEX, selling into strength in the hope of holding the index below 600 and thus avoiding covering positions following heavy options expirations at that level on Friday.

"A lot of people took out Nov 600 calls at the beginning of the month, when the AEX was around 580, basically levering up their view of where the index was heading for a few guilders -- now it looks like paying off and the market makers have to pay up or go into the market and buy stock," a dealer said.
Dealers said Wednesday's U.S. Federal Reserve Open Market Committee meeting could prove crucial for the near term trend of the Dutch share market.
"The best thing that could happen for us is that they leave interest rates unchanged, that way the dollar holds steady and Wall Street goes up and we go with it," said another dealer.
Other dealers said it was only a matter of time before the 600 level falls, as pent up buying demand sweeps prices upwards for basically psychological reasons.
"There's a lot of bets on 600 and we should see it in the next two or three days," one dealer said.

Opinion was divided, however, over the medium term trend of the AEX with some saying a squeeze on market makers scrambling to cover positions after options expirations on Friday could put extra points on the index above 600. Others say recent gloom about disappointing Dutch corporate earnings could dissuade investors in a market which has risen 20.5 percent this year.
